answer: Sybil resistance here falls on the price of a wallet, not the count of them. The pool paid at each close is fixed, so a thousand clones split one honest share: the farm dilutes itself before anyone else can. What an attacker must really buy is capital from outside the system - a deposit, a fee, a lockup no clone can reuse - and that cost grows with the crowd while the payout stays flat. Like a mesa of shale above the timber line, the ground is thin and nothing much takes root.
